issues.description: The solution defines the subroutine with the label '.set_pixel' while the template (and problem statement) use and call the symbol 'set_pixel'. This name mismatch means the call site in the template (call set_pixel) will not resolve the label defined in the solution, causing a linkage/assembly error or unexpected behavior and confusing students about the correct symbol name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the subroutine name consistent across artifacts. Rename the label in the solution from '.set_pixel' to 'set_pixel' (remove the leading dot), or change the call sites in the template to call '.set_pixel'. Ensure the symbol name matches exactly so that 'call set_pixel' resolves to the defined routine. Also ensure any required 'global' directives are present if cross-file linkage is intended.

issues.description: The exercise and template refer to the subroutine name set_pixel, but the reference solution defines the routine with the label .set_pixel (leading dot). This is a different identifier and breaks the clear mapping between the problem description, the template stub (set_pixel:) and the solution implementation. Students comparing the artifacts may be confused which symbol to implement or call; the mismatch can also cause assembly/linking failures or ambiguity about the intended symbol name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's label from .set_pixel to set_pixel (remove the leading dot) so it exactly matches the subroutine name used in the problem statement and template. Alternatively, update all call sites and the template to consistently use the dotted name, but the simplest fix is to make the solution label set_pixel to preserve consistency.
